- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.70 or above) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.40 or below) — model is too conservative, missing downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods — especially when sentiment is volatile, model delays reaction to recent price drops or spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to false peaks or troughs in forecasted 30d path.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.00–0.25), model overestimates — assume slight downward bias unless sentiment is strong.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging — e.g., if price rises but sentiment turns negative, model may continue rising.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often overestimates 30d peak — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high if sentiment is cooling.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model should reduce forecast slope — avoid steep upward revisions unless sentiment reverses sharply.
